answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer, and a non-auto-renewing primary contract expiring in 14 days, an outright primary switch (despite memory_c2's cost win) would raise delivery risk at the worst moment, and negotiate_terms is blocked because the incumbent has already refused to reopen price. Deferral is not safe here because, unlike memory_c5's non-critical renewal, this is primary supply and lapse means interruption. Adding a second source at a guarded partial allocation is the single move that does not disturb incumbent continuity (consistent with memory_c1), directly attacks the single-point-of-failure exposure that memory_c3 indicates held up under shortage, and creates the competitive leverage needed to pursue the mandated 18% cut at the next review without betting the line this cycle. I am verifying memory_c3 because the risk-reduction claim is the load-bearing premise for choosing dual-sourcing over a cost-first switch; I keep allocation small so uncertainty about the new vendor is preserved rather than resolved by commitment.
